t: Founded in 1232 by Muhammad I ibn al-Ahmar, it survived as a tributary of Castile while the rest of al-Andalus fell.
Silk, sugar and dried fruit exported through Málaga and Almería, often by Genoese merchants, sustained a crowded mountain realm.
Civil wars and the Castilian war of 1482–1492 ended it when Boabdil surrendered Granada on 2 January 1492.
dyk: The walls of the Alhambra are inscribed with poems by the court poet Ibn Zamrak, some of which speak in the voice of the building itself.
ev: Ibn al-Ahmar proclaims himself ruler at Arjona
Muhammad I cedes Jaén and becomes a vassal of Ferdinand III of Castile
Castile defeats the Marinids and Yusuf I at the Battle of Río Salado
Muhammad V regains his throne and later builds the Court of the Lions
Castile takes Antequera after a long siege
Málaga falls after a long siege and its people are enslaved
Boabdil surrenders Granada to Isabella I and Ferdinand II on 2 January
